The dedicated-marker connection path now fails instead of skipping when PG 19 is unavailable.
Both containers carry the dedicated label and are tracked by validated full Docker container IDs rather than shell process IDs or name-only cleanup.
Detached runners are bounded with `timeout ... docker wait`; normal, timeout, and SIGKILL paths finalize cleanup before reporting success.
Docker removal and absence-verification failures are fatal and cannot produce destruction or targeted PASS messages.
The normal path parses `go test -json` and requires exactly one test-level PASS for Test_StatAutovacuumScoresQuery_WraparoundException; package-level output alone is insufficient.
The daemon-error control exercises cleanup failures and uses the real Docker client to remove and verify its control containers.
